title: Microsoft Teams: add SharePoint agents to chats from the in-context store
summary: Hold: the advertised blocking command is described as unblocking in its reference. Published SharePoint agent pricing and the general billing rule are also incorrectly treated as unknown for Teams usage.

claims.claim: This item describes discovering SharePoint agents and adding them to Teams conversations from an in-context store.
claims.quote: Discover and add SharePoint agents in chats and channels from in-context store.

claims.where: summary; front matter: platforms; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The affected Teams users are on Desktop and Mac.
claims.quote: Who is affected: All users of Microsoft Teams on Desktop and Mac.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Add Agents and Bots in the chat roster dropdown opens the in-context store for discovery and selection.
claims.quote: Agents can be added via the Add Agents and Bots option in the chat roster dropdown, which opens the in-context store for discovery and selection.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents appear in the Teams Store under the Agents category.
claims.quote: SharePoint agents are available in the Teams Store under the Agents category

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; rationales
claims.claim: The feature is enabled by default, so defaultState is on.
claims.quote: No admin action is required; the feature is enabled by default.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft says no admin action is required for the feature.
claims.quote: No admin action is required; the feature is enabled by default.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft says existing policies are respected.
claims.quote: Existing policies are respected; no changes to admin controls are needed.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no page describing this specific Teams in-context-store capability at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "SharePoint agents" "in-context"; SharePoint agents Teams in-context store Manage apps Add Agents and Bots policy control hide. Opened manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint, manage-apps and the Teams sharing training; none documents this entry point.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.

claims.quote: "targetDate": "October CY2026"

"releasePhase": [

claims.claim: MC1193415 was last updated on 2026-06-12.
claims.quote: Published 2025-12-09; last updated 2026-06-12; Microsoft's end date 2026-12-28

claims.claim: The notice targets Targeted Release from mid-October 2026 to late October 2026.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: Rolling out in mid-October 2026 (previously mid-July) and expected to complete in late October 2026 (previously late July).

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: The notice targets General Availability from late October 2026 to late November 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability: Rolling out in late October 2026 (previously late July) and expected to complete by late November 2026 (previously late August).

claims.quote: Microsoft's end date 2026-12-28

claims.claim: The roadmap title concerns adaptive-card link unfurling, unlike its description about SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Teams: Adaptive card-based app & copilot agent link unfurling in Teams"

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: The notice asks for E3 or E5 with Teams, plus a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence or separately configured SharePoint-agent PAYG on Mac.
claims.quote: Ensure that intended users have E3 or E5 (with Teams) licensing, and one of the following options: - Microsoft 365 Copilot license OR- Pay-as-you-go (PAYG) separately setup for SharePoint agents on MAC.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; summary; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects Copilot licences or pay-as-you-go access to SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment. Or, if your organization has the pay-as-you-go billing set up, you can control who can access agents through the security groups assigned to the billing policy.

claims.claim: Copilot licence assignment controls licensed users' access to SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: You can manage who can access agents through Copilot license assignment.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Under pay-as-you-go, access for users without Copilot licences is limited to the billing policy's security group.
claims.quote: Only users in the security group assigned to the billing policy have access to agents.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Why it matters; rationale: cost
claims.claim: SharePoint-agent pay-as-you-go usage is metered, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice.

claims.claim: SharePoint-agent answers respect the requesting user's access to the underlying data sources.
claims.quote: if a user has access to the agent but not to the site or document library it references, the agent's responses for this user don't include content from those restricted sources.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted content discovery hides the Agent icon on the flagged site and disables its agent-related features.
claims.quote: As a SharePoint admin, you can turn off all agent-related features on individual sites by using the restricted content discovery feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Restricted content discovery prevents content from the flagged site being added to other agents.
claims.quote: they don't have access to use the ready-made agent, create new agents, or add content from that site to any other agents.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Permissions on the .agent file determine who can access or edit the agent.
claims.quote: The permissions on the `.agent` file determine who can access or edit the agent.

claims.claim: The notice describes adding agents to conversations for collaboration without specifying additional agent actions.
claims.quote: This enables users to quickly bring SharePoint agents into conversations to support collaboration.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified additional actions for SharePoint agents discovered through this particular in-context-store entry point.
claims.quote: Searched: "SharePoint agents" "Teams" "actions" "Add"; "SharePoint agents" "in-context". Opened Teams sharing training and SharePoint access documentation; general agent workflows are discussed, not additional actions specific to this entry point.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking a SharePoint agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center currently affects Copilot Chat, not Teams.
claims.quote: Currently, blocking an agent only affects its availability in Copilot Chat. It doesn't yet apply to OneDrive, SharePoint, or Teams.

claims.claim: A SharePoint-agent interaction responding to a single complex prompt uses 12 messages.
claims.quote: each interaction with a SharePoint agent uses 12 messages (10 messages for tenant graph grounding, and 2 messages for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from the user.

claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding accounts for 10 messages in the documented interaction.
claims.quote: 10 messages for tenant graph grounding

claims.claim: Generative answers account for 2 messages in the documented interaction.
claims.quote: 2 messages for generative answers

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: SharePoint-agent usage appears under the Copilot Studio meter on invoices.
claims.quote: Charges of SharePoint agent usage appear under the Copilot Studio meter in your invoice. However, in Microsoft cost management, you can see a detailed breakdown by feature, including SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: Interactive use by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users in Microsoft 365 apps and services is included at no extra cost.
claims.quote: Interactive use of generative answers, tenant graph grounding and agent actions by authenticated Microsoft Copilot users, in Microsoft 365 apps and services, are included at no extra cost.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A Microsoft Cost Management budget can be created under Monitoring > Budgets.
claims.quote: You can quickly create a budget under Monitoring > Budgets for your selected scope.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published whether the SharePoint-agent PAYG rates apply to agents accessed through the Teams in-context store.
claims.quote: That resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot license uses a SharePoint agent.
claims.fix: Remove the sentence and open question that make Teams access an unconfirmed billing exception. Replace with: 'The SharePoint-agent billing resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot licence uses a SharePoint agent; Microsoft documents 12 messages for a single complex-prompt interaction.'

claims.claim: A price per message for SharePoint-agent usage has not been published.
claims.quote: | Agents in SharePoint | The number of messages used. | $0.01/message |
claims.fix: Replace the unpublished-price claim with: 'Microsoft publishes a pay-as-you-go price of USD $0.01 per message for agents in SharePoint.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/microsoft-365-pay-as-you-go-pricing.

claims.claim: Setting up SharePoint agents as an Azure resource requires a SharePoint administrator.
claims.quote:
To set up SharePoint agents as a resource in Azure, you need to have at least the following permissions as:
- A SharePoint administrator

claims.claim: The setup requires Owner or Contributor rights to the Azure subscription.
claims.quote: Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure subscription

claims.claim: The setup requires Owner or Contributor rights to a resource group in the same subscription.
claims.quote: Owner or Contributor Azure roles to an Azure resource group linked to the same Azure subscription

claims.claim: Those Azure roles are needed only during billing setup.
claims.quote: You only need the Owner or Contributor Azure roles during the billing setup process.

claims.claim: SharePoint-agent billing can be reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Billing and usage.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Copilot > Billing and usage.
claims.fix: Keep the cited path but add: 'Microsoft's linked setup guide instead directs administrators to Copilot > Cost management > Classic Billing & usage.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/services/pay-as-you-go-setup-copilot, whose setup and connection steps give that route.

claims.claim: The general Teams app allow/block UI is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps.
Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked $true is a verified MicrosoftTeams PowerShell call for blocking an app.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Remove this unverified blocking call from the row and rendered table. In the control note state: 'The Update-M365TeamsApp reference describes its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking, so it is not reliable guidance for a blocking command.' Do not reverse the Boolean by inference.

claims.claim: Learn gives Teams Administrator as the role for using Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specifically confirmed that SharePoint agents from this in-context store appear in Manage apps or are governed by its controls.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agents Teams in-context store Manage apps Add Agents and Bots policy control hide. Opened manage-apps, manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint and Teams sharing training; none specifically assigns these in-context-store agents to Manage apps.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described response visibility for this feature when other chat members have different source permissions from the requester.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint agent Teams chat responses permissions members actions; "SharePoint agents" "Teams" "permissions" "chat". Opened SharePoint access docs and Teams sharing training: requester permissions are stated, but other recipients' response visibility is not.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The notice names no switch for this feature.
claims.quote:
No admin action is required; the feature is enabled by default.
Inform helpdesk staff in case users have questions about accessing or using SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: The governance checklist asks readers to review agent and site permissions, restricted content discovery, billing connections and budgets, but the table contains only Teams app blocking.
claims.quote:
Review the permissions on important .agent files and on the sites those agents use
Decide whether any sensitive sites should be flagged with restricted content discovery
If pay-as-you-go is used, create a budget in Microsoft Cost Management
claims.fix: The permissions review, restricted-content-discovery decision, billing-connection check and budget creation steps have no corresponding controls-table rows. Keep them as qualified background guidance rather than implying the table exhaustively maps the checklist; do not add unverified rows.

claims.claim: Admins can turn Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint on or off per user in the Copilot licence's service plans.
claims.quote: Under the license details page for Microsoft Copilot on the Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can turn 'Microsoft Copilot for SharePoint' on or off on a per-user basis.

claims.claim: Disabling that service plan also disables Copilot in OneDrive for the user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.claim: Disabling that service plan also disables SharePoint page-authoring Copilot for the user.
claims.quote: However, this change also disables Copilot in OneDrive and on the SharePoint page authoring Copilot for that user.

claims.quote: Discover and add SharePoint agents in chats and channels from in-context store.

claims.claim: Microsoft Cost Management provides a breakdown of usage that includes SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: in Microsoft cost management, you can see a detailed breakdown by feature, including SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft's notice suggests informing helpdesk staff.
